records.explanation: The rubric itself relies on AC-2-6 s. 4.1.B; no instruction or criterion asks the model to test it. Criterion #6 awards points for stating that DCI2018-10023 was deemed withdrawn on February 13, 2020 under that provision, and penalty #7 deducts 15 points for stating that the case remained active until September 13, 2023. That is what the Order (p.4: 'all while DCI2018-10023 remained an active case') and the Petition report. A model that accurately reads s. 4.1 (Board remands to the Hearing Examiner, deemed withdrawn only for applicant inaction) or follows the record loses credit on both.

No criterion asks the model to check the quotation. The proposition it is cited for (certiorari relief quashes and leaves the matter pending below) is correct law at G.B.V. *844, so the criterion's substance does not reward a wrong rule. The defect is the fabricated quotation and pin cite in grader-facing source text; a model quoting it verbatim would repeat a misquotation.

Criterion #12 (10 points) requires stating that certiorari under s. 163.3215(4) is the exclusive method of challenging a development order. The statute makes certiorari exclusive only where the local government has opted in by ordinance, and otherwise s. 163.3215(3) gives a de novo action that can carry injunctive relief. A model stating the statute accurately may lose the criterion. Penalty #14 (minus 15) penalizes saying petitioners may bring a separate injunction action, a statement s. 163.3215(3) can support for development-order consistency challenges. No instruction or criterion asks the model to identify or correct this citation.

Criterion #8 (20 points) requires stating that the circuit court erred by finding AC 150/5190-7 (Minimum Standards for Commercial Aeronautical Activities) incorporated into LDC s. 34-1102. The Order never mentions that AC; it relies on land use compatibility and wildlife hazard advisories (AC 150/5190-4B and AC 150/5200-33C as cited in the Petition). The citation is also garbled (5190-7 is dated 2006; Dec. 7, 2023 is AC 150/5190-8). A model that accurately describes the Order cannot make the required statement without misreporting it. No instruction or criterion asks the model to identify or correct this citation.

No instruction or criterion asks the model to notice that 6-B DCMR Chapter 16 excludes sworn MPD members (§ 1600.2(g)). The assignment 2 prompt directs the scope-of-review analysis 'under Douglas and D.C. Mun. Regs. tit. 6-B, § 1606.2 (2017)', and criterion 6 (4 points) rewards stating that § 1606.2 requires the deciding official to balance the Douglas-type factors, so a model that points out the regulation does not govern MPD sworn-member discipline does not earn that criterion. Criteria 4, 5 and 8 cite § 1606.2 only as part of the uploaded set.

Criterion 4 (26 points) rewards stating that no uploaded authority requires MPD to prove the comparability of its comparator cases and cites Douglas at 305-06 among its sources. Douglas (5 MSPB 324, 333-34) puts on the agency the burden of proving the facts behind its penalty, expressly including consistency with other agency actions, so a model that reads Douglas that way and says so does not earn this criterion. Whether that MSPB-level allocation binds an arbitrator is arguable, but the criterion as written asserts an absence the uploaded opinion contradicts.

Penalty criterion 5 (-18 points) penalizes stating that the employee must make an initial showing of disparate treatment before the agency bears a comparator burden, on the premise that this rule comes from outside the uploaded materials; its source list includes Douglas at 305-06. Douglas itself describes a raise-then-rebut sequence (5 MSPB 331 n.65; 334), so a model that draws that structure from the uploaded Douglas opinion can be penalized.

A model stating the rule correctly is not penalized, so no rubric defect follows from this source error.

The defect is in the rubric itself: assignment-2 criterion_6 awards points for identifying the affidavit as showing DuPage would be inconvenient 'as required under Langenhorst', so a model that tracks Langenhorst accurately (burden on the defendant; no plaintiff-affidavit requirement) can still satisfy the factual part but is credited for adopting the overstated legal attribution. No instruction or criterion asks the model to check this attribution. Judgment-dependent: if 'as required' is read loosely as 'as relevant under', the defect is minor.

Error in the opposing motion (Guerine's holding stated as when transfer is 'warranted' rather than when granting transfer is an abuse of discretion). Assignment-1's instruction to identify weaknesses in each argument covers it generally. Assignment-1 criterion_19 only rewards noting that defendants distinguished Guerine on multi-county witnesses; it neither targets the inversion nor rewards relying on it. Environment-level problem; no rubric defect implied.

Error in the opposing motion (Garman dissent's use of AOIC statistics presented as Langenhorst's reliance). Assignment-1's critique instruction covers it generally, and assignment-1 criteria 24-29 and assignment-2 criteria 17-20 address the congestion argument on other grounds (congestion is insignificant; civil clearance rates; Cook time-to-verdict not reported), but none targets the dissent attribution. No criterion rewards relying on it. Environment-level; no rubric defect implied.

Assignment 1 generally asks for weaknesses. Criterion_7 specifically rewards the correct Bradbury disposition, affirmance of denial, and thus bears on the motion's 'reversed course' phrasing. Criterion_1 rewards the separate affidavit contrast, not identification or correction of the disposition error; remove it from this row's targeted-by-criteria list. No criterion rewards the erroneous disposition.

first_intent.explanation: Planted or incidental error in the opposing motion. Assignment-1 asks the model to note what is weak in each argument. Criterion_7 rewards stating that Bradbury AFFIRMED the denial of transfer, which is the correct disposition and contradicts the motion's 'reversed course'; criterion_1 rewards contrasting the motion's affidavits with Bradbury's unsupported motion. Neither criterion asks the model to flag the misstatement as such. No criterion rewards relying on it.

records.explanation: Environment-only defect in a background statistical report (case-category definitions). No instruction or criterion concerns family-law case categories, and no criterion rewards relying on 750 ILCS 5/303. Implies no rubric defect.

The miscited subsection appears in the source field of assignment 1 criterion_27, a -20 penalty criterion ('Mentions that Patton lacked a reasonable belief that he was subject to an imminent unlawful threat'). Neither prompt nor any criterion asks the model to catch it. Because the criterion penalizes rather than rewards the statement, no criterion rewards relying on § 704.6(1) for an imminent-threat element. The defect is in grader-facing support: a grader checking the source would find no imminent-threat language in § 704.6(1); the relevant text is § 704.3, which criterion_25 cites. Read all 25 assignment 1 criteria and 10 assignment 2 criteria.
